You’re awesome
I love numbers
More specifically data that actually shows me what’s happening
When I have NNLC off it seems that I get higher torque output from vegetarian FoF. Slightly less smooth but better lane changes and turns

Less torque during a NNLC model at a specific speed usually means the model needs to be retrained. I've fixed this with my own NNLC model.
If the previous model is weak at a particular speed you can't use it to train the next NNLC model. Better off training with OP lat.
I’ve been reading into NNLC from the link you provided in another thread. I don’t have a ton of free time right now but when I do I’ll have to start collecting logs for training a model

So after going on a road trip yesterday I can say that vegetarian FoF is my current favorite model for highway driving. It is more aggressive than DTR or any TR models and has higher lane change torque and general torque.

The long for following cars seems good but this model does not do well at stop signs or stoplights for me at all. But given most of my driving is on the highway this is what I’m going to continue to use for the time being.

Yep, this is my new daily.

I go through a roundabout every day when I leave my neighborhood, and it’s been one of the quickest ways to test how well a model handles steering. Most models will understeer that first right turn, which sends the front-left wheel toward the curb. This one either starts turning at the right time, or it knows how far out to swing. Maybe both. Whatever it’s doing, it works.

It’s solid on straight roads, and it handles curves really well too.

If I had to nitpick, I’d say it struggles a bit with sharp 90-degree turns (both left and right). It doesn’t quite commit hard enough, like it’s not totally sure how much to turn. I don’t get any steering or torque limit messages in those moments, so it seems like it's just not going for it.

The only times I do see torque limit messages are when I’m holding the wheel and it’s pushing back a bit, or once on a long right turn on a cloverleaf ramp — and even then, it nailed the turn.

All in all, this model’s at the top of my list right now.
